correctness.rationale: The logarithmic derivative of r⁴(omega−b sin 4theta) cancels the cos 4theta term exactly. Uniform positive radial bounds on P and the strict differential inequality imply forward completeness, attraction, stability and uniqueness of equilibrium. For a C² function at a local minimum, the order-four Lie derivative along the two axes has coefficients (b−a)H11+omega H12 and (b−a)H22−omega H12. Their nonpositivity is impossible for b>a and a positive Hessian. For a strict quadratic both coefficients must be strictly negative, excluding b=a as well. At b=a, r²+P instead is strict and has Hessian 2I; odd positive-definite polynomial degrees cannot occur. This verifies both sharp inequalities with their different equality cases and the semisimple zero Jacobian.
residual_risks: The proof is for a>0 and 0<=b<omega. It does not exclude smooth Lyapunov functions with a degenerate Hessian when b>a, nor classify the angular-locked sector.

evidence: For angular speed B=omega−b sin 4theta>0 the angle invariant law is proportional to B^(-1). The average of cos 4theta is zero by integrating B'/B, so the radial log rate averages −a; the angular GAS criterion covers stability.
Jongeneel's example has nonzero nilpotent linear part and the semisimplicity condition does not exclude a Morse function when the Jacobian is zero.

The later indexed homogeneous criterion says Morse exists iff a positive H has z^T Hf(z)<=0 everywhere. By the symmetry (or the two axes) this is equivalent to b<=a here, but the criterion neither computes the decay identity nor establishes earlier priority.

value.rationale: A stable homogeneous cubic with semisimple zero linearization and an elementary strict polynomial certificate nevertheless loses every local nondegenerate C² certificate at a precise nonlinear boundary. At the boundary it still has a polynomial Morse function but no strict quadratic, separating these notions without changing stability. The exact decay identity makes the example transparent and reusable for Morse-versus-polynomial converse questions.
residual_risks: Scientific value is as an explicit separating family and boundary, not a classification of all homogeneous cubic flows.
